content: Rifampin is associated with an increased risk of endometrial hyperplasia. It decreases the levels of the BCG vaccine live through pharmacodynamic antagonism, making coadministration contraindicated. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of bedaquiline by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug, as strong CYP3A4 inducers can significantly reduce the therapeutic efficacy of bedaquiline. Rifampin decreases bosutinib plasma concentrations by approximately 85% through CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Similarly, rifampin reduces the levels or effects of brigatinib, budesonide, buspirone, cabozantinib, and capivasertib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. For cabozantinib, if coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inducer is unavoidable, increase the cabozantinib dose by 40 mg/day (Cometriq) or 20 mg/day (Cabometyx), and resume the previous dose 2-3 days after discontinuing the inducer. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of capmatinib, carbamazepine, ceritinib, cilostazol, cinacalcet, clozapine, colchicine, conivaptan, conjugated estrogens (oral and vaginal), copanlisib, cortisone, dabigatran, dabrafenib, daridorexant, darifenacin, darolutamide, darunavir, dasatinib, deflazacort, deuruxolitinib, dexamethasone, diazepam, dihydroergotamine (including intranasal), diltiazem, dronedarone, duloxetine, duvelisib, edoxaban, elacestrant, eletriptan, eliglustat, eluxadoline, elvitegravir, encorafenib, entrectinib, enzalutamide, erdafitinib, ergotamine, erlotinib, erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate), estradiol, estrogens (conjugated synthetic), estropipate, ethinyl estradiol, etonogestrel, etrasimod, etravirine, everolimus, fedratinib, felbamate, felodipine, fesoterodine, fexinidazole, finerenone, fludrocortisone, fosamprenavir, fosaprepitant, fostamatinib, and fruquintinib by inducing hepatic and/or intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. For hormonal contraceptives containing ethinyl estradiol, rifampin may reduce their efficacy. It is recommended to use a nonhormonal contraceptive method. Rifampin also decreases systemic exposure to etrasimod, a substrate of CYP3A4, CYP2C8, and CYP2C9. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Rifampin increases the levels or effects of eluxadoline by decreasing its metabolism. If coadministered with OATP1B1 inhibitors, reduce the eluxadoline dose to 75 mg PO BID. Rifampin also increases the levels or effects of enasidenib and erdafitinib by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, separate administration by at least 6 hours before or after administering P-gp substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. For enzalutamide, if coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inducer is unavoidable, increase the enzalutamide dose from 160 mg qDay to 240 mg qDay. If the strong CYP3A4 inducer is discontinued, return to the previous enzalutamide dose. Rifampin is contraindicated with fosamprenavir and everolimus due to significant reductions in their plasma concentrations, which may lead to loss of therapeutic efficacy.
